newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open weaker after Dow fall.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open weaker after Dow fall.

text.p: Singapore shares opened mostly weaker on Thursday following the overnight fall on Wall Street.

"The market looks generally weak this morning. Funds are still sidelined because the Dow looks very unsteady," said a broker with a local firm. The Dow Jones Industrial index fell 45 points to 6,564 overnight.
The broker said retail investors, still reeling from sharp losses sustained in Malaysian shares traded over the counter last week, were still absent from the Signapore bourse.
At 0155 GMT, the Straits Times Industrial Index was down 3.72 points to 2,099.48. Total market volume was 16.4 million shares with 85 losers beating 31 gainers.

There were several early block trades, including Jardine Strategic which saw 1.5 million crossed at around US$3.67. HongKong Land Holdings touched a new 1997 low of US$2.20 in active trading, including about 500,000 shares crossed at around US$2.26.
Singapore Telecom also saw a block deal of 980,000 shares married around S$2.95, down S$0.03. Early gainers included Singapore Press foreign, SIA foreign and Want Want.
